what: *** A DEPARTMENT THIS ARCHIVE HAD NEVER OPENED ***
the query: record index, each of eight spellings exact, q.anyPlace = Artigas, Uruguay
result: *** LERENA 208. Serena 103, Perena 99, Lorena 37, Llerena 32, Larena 28, Gerena 21, Lerina 3. ***
what was already known: Artigas, on the Brazilian border, appears nowhere in this archive's searched list. Everything here assumes the family runs Canelones to Montevideo to Trinidad.
what it means: *** 208 against 699 for FLORES, the known heartland - so Artigas holds roughly a third as many records of this name as the department this archive was built on, and not one of them had been looked at. *** Controlled: the same query at Osaka returns 0.

what: *** AND IT DOES NOT ANSWER THE CENTRAL QUESTION ***
the query: Juan Carlos exact as subject and as father, and Lerena father x Lerena mother, all inside Artigas
what was already known: The department was opened because it was unworked, not because anything pointed a Juan Carlos at it.
what it means: *** No Juan Carlos Lerena at Artigas in any role, and no Lerena-Lerena couple there. *** Recorded as a null rather than left unsaid, because an unworked department is exactly where a reader would assume the archive simply had not looked.

what: *** BENITO LERENA'S HOUSEHOLD, AND WHAT IT COST HIM ***
the query: the 208, read for the man found on act 110 of 1899
result: *** FIVE INFANT DEATHS REGISTERED AT ARTIGAS BETWEEN 1893 AND 1902 ***
what was already known: Benito Lerena was found this morning as the declarant on his grandson's birth act - 45 years old, a jornalero who could not sign his name.
what it means: An unnamed child *** Lerena, died 6 November 1893 ***; another *** died 8 November 1894 ***; *** IDERSIO LERENA ARAUJO, died 19 December 1896 ***; *** GUMERSINDO LERENA, born 1898, died 8 March 1899 ***; and another *** died 25 July 1902. *** Gumersindo died ten weeks before Benito walked into the Juzgado de Paz to register his daughter's son. *** Index-level, every one: no act has been opened. ***

what: *** THE MOTHER THE INDEX COULD NOT NAME ***
the query: the same five deaths, read for the mother's surname
result: *** ARAUJO, CORDERO, CUESTIMA, ARAUJO CARDOZO - and 'Maria Cristina' with no surname at all ***
what was already known: The act of 1899, read at the plate this morning, calls her *** Dona Maria Cristina, 43, brasilera *** and gives her NO SURNAME. That is how the act is written.
what it means: *** FOUR DIFFERENT SURNAMES FOR ONE WOMAN, IN ONE DEPARTMENT, IN NINE YEARS - because the record keeps handing the indexer a woman with one name and the index has a field that must be filled. *** ARAUJO is the likeliest reading: it appears twice, and once as Araujo Cardozo. *** This is the mother-manufacturing failure this archive already documented, caught in the open and five times over. ***

what: *** ANASTASIA'S SECOND SON, EIGHT YEARS ON ***
result: *** TEODORO ALVES LERENA, born 22 April 1907, registered 30 April 1907 at Artigas ***
what was already known: Act 110 of 1899 gave Anastasia Lerena, 22, married to the Brazilian soldier Honorio Alvarez, with one son - Juan Ildebel.
what it means: *** The same couple, eight years later, under the spelling ALVES rather than ALVAREZ. *** So Juan Ildebel and Teodoro are brothers, and the marriage lasted. A third child, *** Crisena Alves ***, is indexed to Honorio with a birth year of 1816 - which in this collection means the year was not read.

what: *** AND TWO MORE LERENA LINES AT ARTIGAS, NEITHER OPENED ***
result: *** DOMINGO LERENA and PEDRO A. LERENA ***
what was already known: Nothing. Neither name is in this register.
what it means: *** DOMINGO LERENA *** with a wife indexed *** Maria Cristina Araujo *** - the same wife-name as Benito's, so either a brother, or one man under two names, or the index conflating two households. Their daughter *** ASUNCION LERENA, b.1884 ***, later living at San Francisco de Asis in Montevideo. And *** PEDRO A. LERENA, born 1827, died 6 November 1896 ***, son of another Pedro A. Lerena and *** Vicenta de la Vega. *** A line running back to the 1790s generation, on the Brazilian frontier. *** All index-level. No act opened, nothing tiered, no connection to this archive's lines shown or claimed. ***
